summary: On September 15, 2024, a team of archaeologists, linguists and local historians unearthed an early 20th-century time capsule beneath the streets of an ancient European crossroads town. It held manuscripts in a regional dialect believed to have faded by the end of the Second World War, plus gramophone discs, photographs and letters. The find is being cataloged and digitized, and it highlights the fragility of linguistic diversity and the need for proactive language preservation.
one_line: A 2024 time capsule find in a European town yields early 20th-century manuscripts, recordings and photographs preserving a vanished regional dialect.
key_facts: The time capsule was uncovered on the morning of September 15, 2024, beneath the cobbled streets of an ancient town in the heart of Europe.
The capsule dates back to the early 20th century and contained manuscripts that may unlock lost languages and dialects.
Dr. Elise Martin, a renowned polyglot and lead linguist, was the first to flip through the pages and called it "the linguistic equivalent of striking gold."
The manuscripts appear to be in a dialect of a regional language that modern linguists believed had faded into silence by the end of the Second World War.
One manuscript, bound in leather with a rusty clasp, holds folklore, accounts of daily life and personal anecdotes, suggesting its author knew the language was endangered.
The capsule also held gramophone disc recordings, photographs of locals conversing, and letters giving real-life context to the language.
The recordings and photographs are keys to the intonation, rhythm and sounds of the language when spoken.
Matthew Harris, the archivist responsible for digitizing the find, plans to use 3D imaging and virtual reality so people worldwide can experience the discovery.
The collection is expected to show how people used language to define cultural boundaries, establish social hierarchies and navigate relationships between groups.
The article says many languages worldwide face threats from globalization, migration and the homogenization of culture.
A folklore story in the manuscripts tells of heroes and myths that shaped the social fabric of the time.
Some manuscript words were marked as endangered at the time of writing and now serve as a lesson in linguistic preservation.
